title: Quarterly growth threads and evidence
content:
Purpose: quick, portable scratchpad for the quarter — capture measurable goals, supporting evidence, manager conversation bullets, and ask-list. Use this ahead of weekly 1:1s and for the mid-cycle growth discussion.

Top-level goals (Q2 2025) — anchor statements
- Reduce time-to-offer (end-to-end) for engineering IC roles from baseline ~38 days to <=28 days. Measure: median days from first intro screen to offer accepted.
- Launch hiring playbook v0 for Platform & Serving teams (templates, scorecards, calibrated interview rubrics) — publish to Confluence and run two hiring calibration sessions with interview panel leads.
- Improve candidate experience NPS for final-round candidates (target +20) via faster feedback loops and clearer next-step comms.
- Manager enablement: build a 60-minute onboarding slice for new managers on "calibrated interviews and bias mitigation" and pilot with two recent hires.

Why these matter (short rationale)
- Our platform roles are high-impact and currently bottlenecked by slow loop and inconsistent rubric use. Tightening the loop = faster product iteration and lower recruiter load.
- A single playbook reduces variance between hiring teams and makes scaling Dedicated/Private hiring easier as we grow in EMEA.

Metrics & current baseline (notes)
- Baseline median time-to-offer (eng): 38 days (measured Jan–Apr 2025). Source: internal hiring metrics spreadsheet.
- Candidate NPS last quarter: +7 (n=45 final-round replies).
- Interview completion rate: ~85% of scheduled interviews run (15% cancel reschedule rate causing delays).

Concrete deliverables and timeline
- May 12–23: Draft interview scorecards + example rubrics for Platform, Serving Runtime, and Console teams. (Done: initial drafts, still rough.)
- Week of May 26: Calibration session #1 with Platform hiring leads — collect feedback and iterate.
- June 9: Publish playbook v0 to Confluence (linked artifact above).
- June 16–30: Pilot manager enablement session with two new managers; collect survey feedback.

Evidence log (for performance notes) — pasteable snippets
- May 8: Led mini-workshop with 8 interviewers on behavioral anchors; post-survey rating 4.1/5, qualitative notes: "more clarity on must-have vs nice-to-have". Link: slack thread.
- May 22: Reduced recruiter triage backlog by 18 requests after triage template introduced (JIRA-HR-342).
- Jun 2: Draft playbook uploaded to Confluence, comments from Priya + Evan, 12 inline suggestions.
- Jun 10: Pilot manager session: 6/6 attendees said they felt 'more confident' in giving calibrated feedback (survey).

Self-assessment bullets (how I see impact)
- Strengths: operationalized several small processes into templates that save ~2–4 hours/week for recruiting team; strong cross-team coordination.
- Growth area: need to push harder on enforcement (follow-up) — playbooks won't be used unless managers and hiring leads commit to them.
- Personal development: want to practice facilitation skills (2 more workshops this quarter), and take a short course on structured de-biasing methods.

Manager conversation agenda (prep for next 1:1)
1) Quick sync (5m): status on metric movement (time-to-offer, NPS).
2) Ask for support (10m): leadership ask — can you lobby Eng Directors to require scorecards for all on-site candidates this quarter? I want explicit buy-in.
3) Resource ask (10m): propose one hire headcount for a recruiting coordinator (contractor) to reduce admin friction — ROI: estimate 8–10 hours/week freed for each recruiter.
4) Feedback (10m): solicit upward feedback on my prioritization and visibility — examples I want input on: the playbook rollout cadence, and whether I should own calibration for EMEA too.
5) Career check (10m): highlight stretch goals and ask for coaching time to practice facilitation.

Specific asks / action items for manager (short list)
- Introduce me to Eng Director of Platform and ask them to sponsor the playbook requirement.
- Approve a 3-month contractor for recruiting coordination (budget ballpark: $6–8k/mo).
- Schedule a 30-minute coaching session with you focused on facilitation techniques before July.

Potential risks & mitigation
- Risk: low adoption of playbook. Mitigation: schedule mandatory 30-min calibration for each hiring squad in the first 6 weeks after publish; follow-up survey.
- Risk: recruiter bandwidth constraints. Mitigation: triage template + one contractor; push more async communication.

Notes to self / scratch ideas (informal)
- Try a "ship small" approach: publish just scorecards + one example role template first, then roll out rubrics.
- Consider a short "interview cadence cheat sheet" for candidates to reduce reschedules.
- Keep a running list of interviewers who are strong calibrators (potential future panel leads).

Draft language for status update to manager (one-paragraph)
- "Quick update: playbook v0 is live in draft form on Confluence. Ran the first calibration with Platform leads; feedback was actionable and I've already incorporated 12 suggestions. Early signals: recruiter triage backlog fell and interviewer prep ratings improved in the workshop. Next steps: finalize v0, run manager enablement pilots, and seek your support to formalize scorecard use for upcoming hiring rounds.

Questions I want answered in 1:1
- Are you comfortable sponsoring the scorecard requirement with Eng Directors?
- Is a 3-month contractor for recruiting coordination reasonable or should I propose a longer ramp?
- Would you like monthly snapshot emails from me on hiring metrics (or prefer dashboards only)?

Todo (short)
- [ ] Finalize playbook edits and merge comments (due Jun 6)
- [ ] Schedule second calibration with Serving team (target Jun 12)
- [ ] Prepare facilitator notes for manager enablement pilot (due Jun 9)
- [ ] Draft hiring coordinator budget justification (due Jun 18)

Random mental notes (scratch)
- Burnout signals on one recruiter — escalate to Priya for bandwidth review.
- Candidate feedback: some confusion about "next steps" timeline in offer stage. Could add a simple 3-step candidate comms template.

End of doc — quick snapshot for mid-cycle review.

(Keep iterating; this is intentionally terse and imperfect.)
